subject: Post-demo: unexpected variant drift after model update — proposed action ladder
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + variant drift we saw (short)

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the candid feedback. Quick recap from our side and a short request:

What we observed
- After the model deploy on 2027-08-01 (variant v2027-08-01-alpha), a small but reproducible change in token-level outputs showed up for the authorization-reason prompts in your test set (higher hallucination rate on 3 of 25 cases).
- Customer-facing flows you demoed were otherwise stable, but QA flagged the 3 examples as a regression from the v2027-07-28 baseline.

Immediate ask
- Can you confirm whether your sandbox traffic includes the updated variant? If possible, keep a short window of traffic pinned to the previous variant so we can compare logs.

Next steps we propose
1) We'll run a quick diff and share a short eval artifact (prompt sets + diff report).
2) If the diff confirms a regression, propose an action ladder: temporary pin -> traffic split 90/10 -> rollback if necessary.
3) Schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to align on what to pin and timeline.

I'll attach the initial artifacts once they finish processing (should be ~60 minutes). If you want to move faster, let us know and we can prioritize a hotfix rollback.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none yet]

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmepayments.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Payments Ops <ops@acmepayments.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + variant drift we saw (short)

Thanks Marcus — we did notice a change in a small subset of authorization messages this morning. Confirmed: our staging cluster was routed to the new variant starting 2027-08-01 02:00 UTC.

Impact for us:
- The three failure examples you mentioned are hitting a small portion (~2%) of live traffic in staging. Production is still on the previous baseline for now.
- This is time-sensitive since we go wide to production next week; we can't have regressions in approval language.

Agree with your proposed ladder. Can you share the diff and a quick suggested rollback/pin plan? If you recommend rolling back, we'll need an ETA and a note for our change control.

— Liam
Head of Product, Acme Payments

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + variant drift we saw (short)

Hi Liam — thanks for the quick confirmation. We finished an initial automated diff and a short manual pass; attaching the artifacts for your dev/ops team:

Attachments
- eval_diff_report.pdf (contains side-by-side token diffs and a 25-case samplesheet)
- prompt_suite_v3.json (the 120 prompt variants we used for the regression check)
- benchmarks-20270802.csv (aggregate metrics: hallucination-rate, answer-length, confidence score)

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- The new variant v2027-08-01-alpha increases hallucination rate on the authorization prompt family from 1.2% -> 4.8% (absolute +3.6 pp), concentrated in three edge-case templates.
- Overall throughput/latency is unchanged; cost per token is modestly lower due to quantization kernels, which likely motivated the update.

Recommended action ladder (low friction to high friction)
1) Pin: Set production routing to the v2027-07-28-stable variant (we can pin at service-level immediately). This gives you the previously validated baseline while we investigate.
2) Canary split: If you prefer no immediate pin, do a 90/10 traffic split (90% baseline /10% new) for 24–48 hours to collect more samples.
3) Rollback: If the 90/10 still shows the drift or you see customer impact, rollback the deploy and open a remediation ticket with our runtime team.

We can implement 1) within 30 minutes with approval from your ops lead. To make the decision easier, here are quick links:
- Diff report: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cEvalReport
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/12487

Notes about pinning: pinning only affects routing; the variant remains available for testing. If you want us to pin, tell us which service name + environment and we'll apply it and send a change ticket.

If helpful, I can run a focused 60-minute QA pass on the three failing examples (manual rewrite + counterfactual prompts) and deliver proposed fix prompts in ~4 hours.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: eval_diff_report.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)]
[Attachment: prompt_suite_v3.json (JSON, 42KB)]
[Attachment: benchmarks-20270802.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acmepayments.com>, Acme Payments Ops <ops@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2027 14:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + variant drift we saw (short)

Liam — appreciate the quick turnaround from your team. From a commercial/ops standpoint:
- If you want an immediate pin to v2027-07-28-stable, we can do that now; it will pause the performance rollout but won't change pricing or license terms.
- If you choose rollback later (after 90/10), we'll coordinate a scheduled rollback window; our SREs will own the change and provide a post-mortem.

Requested confirmation items (so we can action fast):
1) Confirm pin now? Reply with the exact service name and "pin: v2027-07-28-stable" and we'll apply.
2) If you need a formal change request + signature for your audit, sign the attached change approval (DocuSign link) and we'll treat as green-light.

DocuSign (change request): https://www.docusign.com/some/signature/DEAL-12487-change-request
Priority note: given your go-wide timeline next week, our recommendation is to pin and run the 90/10 in staging while Monica runs the targeted QA pass. That preserves momentum while minimizing risk.

Thanks — I'll stand by for your confirmation.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
